shop/steps

What it is
  Every way a step is said: by itself, by its action, and by the language.
  It keeps, from one run to the next: `last`, `open` and `seen`.
  What it is doing is written down as it goes, so that it is taken up where it was after a restart.
  Whoever applies it may tell it 2 things:
    - count: How many there are. Unless it is said: `2`.
    - mode: Its text does not say what it is for. One of `plain` or `fancy`. Unless it is said: `plain`.

What it does when it is applied
  1. Look at the thing first. [said]
  2. Send a letter. [unsaid]
  3. Read a thing. [empty]
  4. Say `shop.told`. [told]
  5. Keep `last` and `seen`. [kept]
  6. Wait 5 minutes. [paused]
  7. Say `shop.asked`, and wait until `shop.answered` is said, for 1 hour at most. [asked]
  8. Send a letter. Only when what it keeps as `seen` is not so. [once]
  9. Write a line in the run's log. Only when the step `unsaid` failed. [failed]
  10. Send a letter. Only when the param `count` is more than `3` and the param `mode` is `fancy`. [many]
  11. Send a letter. Only when the param `mode` is one of `plain` or `fancy` or what it keeps as `last` says something. [either]
  12. Send a letter. Only when a condition holds, written `len(params.mode) > 3`. [worked]
  13. Two things done as one. [group]
    1. Read a thing. [group.inner]
    2. And said. [group.after]
  14. Keep an entry in its list `open`. [held]
  15. Take an entry out of its list `open`. [let_go]
  16. Measure `shop.counted`. [counted]
  17. Do nothing. [nothing]
  18. Stop `helper` and everything it started. [child]
  19. Fail here, on purpose. Only when the param `count` is less than `0`. [wrong]
  20. End this run here, as failed. [over]

What it may do
  It runs as whoever applies it, and can do no more than they can.
  Of what they can do, it uses only what it lists: `things` and `post`.
  Read things. [things:read]
  Send letters. [post:send]
